transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I'm here because... well, things at work have been difficult. I keep hearing people talking about me. Through the conference room walls... or sometimes from my phone, even when it's turned off. 

It's usually the board members, or my staff. They're... they're saying I'm ruining the company. It just sounds so clear that I actually answer them back. Before I realize that... no one else heard it.
How long have you been hearing these voices—did this start recently, or has it been going on for weeks or months?
I suppose... it's been about three months. Yeah, around three months since it started with the walls and the phone.
During these past three months, have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, or other recreational drugs?
No... I haven't. I don't use anything like that. Just... no.

Over these past three months, have you noticed a significant change in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or low most of the day, or on the other hand, feeling unusually energetic, elated, or needing less sleep than usual?
I don't... no. I haven't really noticed anything like that. My mood is... fine, I suppose. I'm just trying to deal with... everything at work. But no.

Aside from these experiences, have you noticed any changes in yourself lately—like losing interest in things you used to enjoy, feeling less motivated, withdrawing from friends or family, or having a harder time keeping up with your usual daily activities?

I suppose... things are different. I used to be the one driving every idea, you know? Always calling people after openings. Now... I just sit at my desk for hours. Staring at the agenda. I don't really talk to my husband much anymore, or the staff. And the work I used to love... I just don't feel much about it now. It's just... empty.
You mentioned feeling withdrawn and less motivated at work—when did you first start noticing these changes, compared to when the voices began three months ago?

Long before that. It's... it's been building for a while now. Maybe two years and four months ago. That was when the company expanded... they put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division. I suppose... that's when it started.
Since these changes in motivation and withdrawal began over two years ago, have they been present continuously, without any significant breaks or return to your normal self, up until now?
I don't... I'm not really sure. It's hard to keep track of time like that. It all just blends together, I suppose. I haven't really thought about whether there were breaks.

Thinking back over the past several months, would you say you've had at least some signs of this withdrawal or low motivation nearly every day for six months or more in a row, even before the voices started?
I suppose... yes. It's been a long time. Just... day after day. Like I said, it just blends.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports auditory hallucinations (voices through walls/phone) with associated delusional content (belief board members/staff are conspiring against her, ruining the company) for approximately 3 months, occurring in clear sensorium without substance use. These positive symptoms are accompanied by a longer-standing (~2 years 4 months) prodromal/negative symptom phase characterized by anhedonia, social withdrawal, avolition, and functional decline (withdrawal from spouse and staff, loss of interest in work she previously loved), present nearly daily for well over 6 months. No manic or depressive mood episode was identified concurrent with psychotic symptoms, arguing against schizoaffective disorder or mood disorder with psychotic features. The combination of characteristic positive symptoms (hallucinations, delusions) plus prominent negative symptoms with functional deterioration exceeding 6 months meets criteria for schizophrenia.
